The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic sine function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5\operatorname{arsinh}⁡(3x)) \\  & =5\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsinh}⁡(3x)) \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{(3x)^{2}+1}}\cdot (3x)^{′} \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{9{x}^{2}+1}}\cdot 3 \\  & =\frac{15}{\sqrt{9{x}^{2}+1}}.\end{aligned}
$$
